reasons: The best candidate's result rests on a degenerate metric: only 2 downside sessions out of 384, far below the pre-registered threshold of 5. The strategy was scored on Sharpe instead of Sortino, meaning the denominator (downside volatility) is estimated from almost nothing and is unreliable.

The validation split shows catastrophic degradation: train Sharpe = -0.0125, validation Sharpe = -0.1516, a change of -0.139. The strategy loses money on both splits (train net PnL = -0.70, validation net PnL = -1.65) and shows a win rate of 0% on validation with only 2 trades.

Extreme concentration in validation: the strategy executed only 2 trades across 86 sessions (2.3% of sessions had exposure). Both trades lost money. A result from 2 trades is not a statistic; it is a pair of outcomes.

The null distribution shows the observed best score (-0.0125) is far below the null mean (0.053) and well below even the 50th percentile of the null max (0.067). The gate p-value is 0.987, indicating the result is indistinguishable from random noise.

Validation diagnostics reveal extreme concentration by time: all losses occur in 2 months (Feb and Apr 2026) and 2 specific hours (14:00 and 20:00 UTC). This pattern suggests the result is an artifact of a handful of market conditions rather than a generalizable strategy.
auditors.confidence_note: I cannot see the strategy code or how candidates were generated, so I cannot assess whether the search process itself was sound; however, the statistical evidence on this axis is unambiguous.

reasons: The strategy has negative net P&L on both train (-0.70 points) and validation (-1.65 points) after commission. Gross P&L is +0.90 points on train but commission paid is 1.60 points, making the net result -0.70 points. This is not an edge; it is a cost artifact.

Commission as a fraction of gross P&L is 178% on train (1.6 / 0.9) and 128% on validation (0.4 / -1.25). The strategy does not pay for itself. On 8 trades over 384 sessions, the strategy is losing money to transaction costs.

Trade count is degenerate: 8 trades across 384 sessions (0.021 trades per session) on train, and 2 trades across 86 sessions (0.023 trades per session) on validation. This is not a signal; this is inactivity. A strategy that trades almost never will score well when activity is costly, and that is what has happened here.

The validation result is substantially worse than train (Sharpe -0.152 vs -0.013), and the strategy fires only 2 times on the validation set. With 2 trades and 86 sessions, the result is noise, not a discovery. The win rate on validation is 0%.

The hypothesis claims absorption marks a turn and initiation confirms it. The code requires 3 consecutive initiation bars after absorption before entering (initiation_bars_required=3). This is a multi-bar confirmation that is so strict it filters out almost all signal. The docstring acknowledges trial #15 was 'too restrictive' with prior-bar confirmation, but the solution — requiring 3 consecutive initiation bars — is even more restrictive. The strategy has collapsed to near-zero activity.

The hypothesis is economically plausible in principle (orderflow reversals are real), but this implementation does not test it. It tests whether a 3-bar confirmation filter on top of absorption detection produces a profitable strategy. It does not. The filter has killed the signal without improving the edge.
auditors.confidence_note: I cannot see whether the absorption and initiation detection logic correctly implements the hypothesis as written, or whether the delta thresholds and prior-bar confirmation are sound. I can see that the strategy as deployed trades almost never and loses money to commission, which is sufficient to veto on economic grounds regardless of the signal quality.

reasons: Extreme concentration in single trades: only 2 trades executed on validation (86 sessions), with 0% win rate and -1.65 net PnL. The strategy is not a repeatable pattern but a pair of losing bets.

Validation performance is a mirror image of training: train primary -0.0125, validation primary -0.1516. The 139bp deterioration (rule_c) combined with negative validation Sharpe and Sortino indicates the strategy does not generalize; this is not noise but systematic failure.
Validation shows only 2 sessions with exposure out of 86 sessions. This is not a strategy; it is two isolated trades. No basis to assess robustness across conditions.
Training data shows 8 trades across 384 sessions with best_session_share of 16.7% and profit_concentration_top5pct of 1.0 — all profit comes from one session. Removing that session flips the sign.
Kurtosis of 41.8 on validation indicates extreme tail risk and non-normal returns, consistent with a strategy that fires rarely and unpredictably rather than a robust repeatable signal.

By-month and by-hour breakdowns on validation show all losses concentrated in 2026-02 (Mon, 14 UTC) and 2026-04 (Thu, 20 UTC) — only two data points, each a single trade. No evidence of broad-based behavior.
auditors.confidence_note: You cannot see out-of-sample results, but the validation split itself shows the strategy is not robust: it executes almost no trades, loses on both, and exhibits extreme concentration. The training-to-validation deterioration is severe and systematic, not sampling noise.
